# Fixtures for scripts/mktemp-template_test.sh — they pin the precision of the matcher.
#
# Format: <verdict><TAB><the source line, verbatim>. A line that starts with # at column 0 is a
# comment, and an empty line is ignored. The 3 verdicts are:
#   none  the line holds no mktemp invocation in command position (prose, a comment, a message)
#   ok    an mktemp invocation that passes no template, or 1 template with >= 3 trailing X's
#   bad   an mktemp invocation that GNU mktemp exits 1 on: a template with fewer than 3 trailing
#         X's ("too few X's in template") or a second template operand ("too many templates")
#
# Every bad row below was read from real GNU mktemp (coreutils 9.4, ghcr.io/gophersys/base), not
# from the manual page.
#
# This file carries the word mktemp on purpose, including the broken forms. It is not a shell
# script and has no shell shebang, so the repository scan of mktemp-template_test.sh never reads
# it — the scan set is shell files only.

# --- not an invocation: mktemp appears as prose ---
none	# every mktemp invocation must carry a template with at least 3 trailing X's
none	printf 'the BSD spelling is mktemp -t prefix\n'
none	#   bash scripts/assert-no-skipped-tests.sh -tags integration -race ./...
none	log="$(make_temporary_file)"

# --- a whole-line comment is never executed, whatever it quotes ---
none	# sudo mktemp -t bad — the broken form, quoted in a comment on purpose
none	#   trap "mktemp -t bad" EXIT

# --- an invocation with no template ---
ok	mktemp
ok	tmp="$(mktemp)"
ok	dir="$(mktemp -d)"
ok	if ! mktemp --version >/dev/null; then
ok	version="$(mktemp --version 2>&1)"

# --- an invocation with a portable template ---
ok	profile="$(mktemp -t agent-runtime-cover.XXXXXX)"
ok	work="$(mktemp -d -t eden-scan.XXXXXX)"
ok	mktemp -p /tmp eden-scan.XXXXXX
ok	mktemp --tmpdir=/var/tmp eden-scan.XXXXXX
ok	mktemp "${directory}/eden-scan.XXXXXX"
ok	mktemp -u eden-scan.XXX

# --- the word mktemp also opens a variable name; only the invocation counts ---
ok	mktemp_version="$(mktemp --version 2>&1)" && mktemp_version_status=0 || mktemp_version_status=$?
none	mktemp_version_status=1
none	printf 'mktemp %s\n' "$mktemp_version"

# --- two invocations on one line: every one of them is judged ---
ok	a="$(mktemp -d)"; b="$(mktemp -t eden-scan.XXXXXX)"
bad	a="$(mktemp -d -t good.XXXXXX)"; b="$(mktemp -t bad-one)"

# --- an invocation whose template GNU mktemp rejects ---
bad	log="$(mktemp -t assert-no-skipped-tests)"
bad	mktemp -t eden-scan
bad	mktemp /tmp/eden-scan
bad	mktemp -d /tmp/eden-scan.XX
bad	mktemp -p /tmp eden-scan
bad	dir="$(mktemp -d -t eden-scan.X)"

# --- --tmpdir carries an OPTIONAL argument: it attaches only with =, and never eats the next word.
# --- `mktemp --tmpdir bad` is rc=1 "too few X's in template"; `mktemp --tmpdir /var/tmp x.XXXXXX`
# --- is rc=1 "too many templates". --suffix and -p do take the next word (required argument).
bad	mktemp --tmpdir bad
ok	mktemp --tmpdir eden-scan.XXXXXX
bad	mktemp --tmpdir /var/tmp eden-scan.XXXXXX
ok	mktemp --tmpdir=/var/tmp -d eden-scan.XXXXXX
bad	mktemp --suffix .json eden-scan
ok	mktemp --suffix .json eden-scan.XXXXXX

# --- GNU accepts 1 template operand at most: a second one is rc=1 "too many templates" ---
bad	mktemp a.XXXXXX b.XXXXXX
ok	mktemp a.XXXXXX
bad	mktemp -p /tmp a.XXXXXX b.XXXXXX
ok	mktemp -p /tmp a.XXXXXX

# --- a leader that opens a command: a shell keyword, a wrapper, a trapped command string ---
bad	if true; then mktemp -t bad; fi
ok	if true; then mktemp -t good.XXXXXX; fi
bad	for f in a b; do mktemp -t bad; done
ok	for f in a b; do mktemp -t good.XXXXXX; done
bad	if mktemp -t bad; then :; fi
ok	if mktemp -t good.XXXXXX; then :; fi
bad	sudo mktemp -t bad
ok	sudo mktemp -t good.XXXXXX
bad	exec mktemp -t bad
ok	exec mktemp -t good.XXXXXX
bad	command mktemp -t bad
ok	command mktemp -t good.XXXXXX
bad	trap "mktemp -t bad" EXIT
ok	trap "mktemp -d -t good.XXXXXX" EXIT
bad	trap 'mktemp -t bad' EXIT
ok	trap 'mktemp -d -t good.XXXXXX' EXIT
